phases.title: Foundations
phases.goal: Trace a browser request from name resolution through transport, HTTP, and browser policy; operate a reproducible local web lab.
phases.exit: Explain and capture one complete HTTPS request, compare HTTP versions, demonstrate a browser policy boundary, and rebuild the local lab from notes.

phases.title: Frontend
phases.goal: Build and inspect browser applications, their dependency graph, and client-side trust boundaries.
phases.exit: Build a small typed frontend, inspect its production bundle, and demonstrate DOM, messaging, worker, and WebSocket boundaries in a local lab.

phases.title: Backend
phases.goal: Build, trace, and secure request handling across common runtimes, frameworks, API styles, and web servers.
phases.exit: Complete each pair's build and security exercises; trace routing, validation, serialization, authorization, and errors in a representative API behind a web server.

phases.title: Data
phases.goal: Understand storage and messaging semantics, query boundaries, access controls, and failure modes.
phases.exit: Complete each storage pair's exercises, demonstrate parameterized queries and least-privilege access, and explain transaction, consistency, and queue delivery tradeoffs.
labs: Local disposable databases, storage emulators, and message brokers

phases.title: Identity
phases.goal: Trace authentication and authorization protocols, credentials, sessions, and token trust decisions.
phases.exit: Diagram each identity flow, validate issuer/audience/state/nonce where applicable, and complete representative session, JWT, OAuth, and MFA labs.
labs: Local test identity provider and relying-party applications

phases.title: Infra and Cloud
phases.goal: Deploy isolated applications with explicit infrastructure, identity, network, cache, and supply-chain boundaries.
phases.exit: Build a reproducible deployment, verify secrets and least-privilege policy, explain proxy/cache behavior, and complete each infrastructure pair's local or sandbox exercise.
labs: [AWS Workshops](https://workshops.aws/) and [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/): dedicated sandbox subscriptions with budgets

phases.title: Attacks
phases.goal: Recognize cross-technology vulnerability classes and validate root causes, impact, and fixes in authorized labs.
phases.exit: Complete all available PortSwigger Apprentice labs relevant to this phase, plus at least one suitable local or Academy lab for every remaining technique; explain each root cause and remediation.

phases.title: Methodology
phases.goal: Run a scoped, repeatable web assessment and communicate evidence, impact, and remediation clearly.
phases.exit: Deliver one authorized end-to-end assessment writeup with scope, reproducible findings, evidence, remediation, and retest results.
labs: An authorized HTB web target or local vulnerable application
A source review of a small local application

phases.title: Foundations
phases.goal: Read x64 code and the Windows ABI, build small native programs, and prepare isolated user-mode, AD, and kernel-debug labs.
phases.exit: Build and inspect a native executable, explain a call at the ABI level, and verify snapshots, isolation, symbols, and a kernel-debug connection using the central WinDbg note.

phases.title: User-mode Internals
phases.goal: Explain user-mode objects, process state, security decisions, system interfaces, and telemetry without revisiting page tables.
phases.exit: Complete each pair's observation exercise; trace a process, module load, handle access check, IPC exchange, and event record using documented evidence.
labs: Small self-authored Win32 programs in a snapshot-backed VM

phases.title: Kernel and Platform
phases.goal: Understand kernel execution constraints, driver interfaces, boot trust, virtualization protections, and supported extension points.
phases.exit: Trace a benign driver's I/O path, explain IRQL and callback constraints, and verify boot and virtualization protections in a disposable VM.
labs: [HEVD](https://github.com/hacksysteam/HackSysExtremeVulnerableDriver): interface study in an isolated VM

phases.title: Development
phases.goal: Build observable Windows automation, managed applications, native programs, COM components, and drivers.
phases.exit: Complete each pair's build exercises, test input and privilege boundaries, and explain the relevant runtime, resource-lifetime, and deployment rules.
labs: Local PowerShell, .NET, Win32, and COM exercises

phases.title: Enterprise
phases.goal: Trace enterprise identity, remote administration, directory, certificate, and policy protocols across trust boundaries.
phases.exit: In a disposable AD lab, trace logon and service authentication, inspect directory and certificate permissions, and verify remote-management and policy hardening.

phases.title: Offensive
phases.goal: Understand Windows and AD attack prerequisites and observable behavior using explicitly authorized disposable labs.
phases.exit: Complete a controlled lab for every technique, identify prerequisite permissions and telemetry, and demonstrate a relevant mitigation or detection with cleanup.
labs: [HTB Academy](https://academy.hackthebox.com/): relevant CPTS/CAPE path modules where available

phases.title: Exploit Dev
phases.goal: Analyze memory-corruption primitives, mitigations, and exploitability in isolated educational binaries and drivers.
phases.exit: Document reproducible user-mode and HEVD lab cases, explain the primitive and applicable mitigations, and complete a static/dynamic analysis writeup without handling production targets.
labs: [Exploit Education](https://exploit.education/) and [Corelan](https://www.corelan.be/): relevant fundamentals and Windows exercises
Dedicated offline malware-analysis VM using vetted training samples

phases.title: Defense
phases.goal: Deploy Windows prevention and telemetry controls, understand their limitations, and verify detection and hardening outcomes.
phases.exit: Apply a test baseline, collect representative telemetry, validate Sigma/KQL detections, and document a controlled limitation test and compensating control for each pair.
